newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast takes aim at new B.C. gas players.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast takes aim at new B.C. gas players.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc is adding to its natural gas processing capacity in northeast British Columbia in reaction to new players vying for its dominant position in the province's gas industry, Westcoast field services president Irv Koop said on Monday.
"We've had to put these solutions in place in order to stave off some competition in the area," Koop said in a telephone interview.
"But the key thing is we're retaining that gas within B.C. so it will continue to move through the existing B.C. infrastructure."
Westcoast said on Monday it planned to build a new natural gas plant in the Highway area of northeast British Columbia and expand its under-construction Jedney plant in the province.
Both projects, located in the Fort St. John area, were estimated to cost over C$100 million.
The projects were announced as competition heats up for processing and pipeline capacity in the gas-rich region.

Novagas Clearinghouse, owned by Calgary-based NOVA corp and NGC Corp of Houston, announced this summer it plans to build a 40 million cubic feet per day plant in northeast B.C.'s Caribou area, where Norcen Energy Resources Ltd is a major gas developer.
The gas would be shipped from the plant to Alberta, where it would be transported on NOVA's intra-Alberta network.
"(Caribou is) right in the midst of where we're putting these other plants," Koop said. "We've reacted to that competition. We've been able to attract customers to our facilities."

Early this year, Westcoast mothballed two projects aimed at boosting transport and processing capacity by more than 400 million cubic feet a day, despite winning a jurisdictional battle against Canada's National Energy Board.
The company said its plans changed during the court dispute as producers, reacting to low natural gas prices in British Columbia, shelved development plans.

Koop said several smaller projects, including the non-NEB regulated ones announced Monday and a debottlenecking of the 700 MMCFD McMahon plant, were undertaken after the major gas plant plans were dropped.
Taken together, the initiatives were expected to add 250 to 275 MMCFD of new capacity to Westcoast's system, he said.
